country.name: Uzbekistan
country.tagline: A vast Silk Road vineyard of table grapes and raisins, with Samarkand's nineteenth-century winery still making sweet fortified wines.

stats.note: OIV 2025: 125 kha of vines, the 14th largest vineyard area in the world, overwhelmingly table grapes and raisins; wine output small and not reported.

country.overview:
Grapes have grown in the oases of Transoxiana for thousands of years. Chinese envoys of the Han dynasty described the wine of Ferghana in the second century BC, Sogdian merchants carried wine and vines along the Silk Road, and Samarkand and Bukhara were famous for their grapes long after Islam made wine a matter of poetry rather than commerce.

The modern industry arrived with the Russian Empire. In Samarkand, a winery founded in 1868 according to its own history by the merchant D. M. Filatov became, in Soviet times, the Khovrenko winery, named after the oenologist M. A. Khovrenko, who led it and developed its range. It is known for sweet and fortified wines in the Soviet style, such as Gulyakandoz, Shirin and Aleatiko, made from grapes grown in a hot continental climate with very high sugar, and for its museum and tasting room. In the Soviet era Uzbekistan was a major source of dessert wines and brandy for the USSR.

Today Uzbekistan has one of the world's largest vineyards by area (about 125,000 hectares, the 14th largest according to the OIV), but almost all of it is for table grapes and raisins, and the wine sector is small. Since the late 2010s the government has opened the economy and encouraged private wineries and wine tourism around Tashkent (Parkent, Bostanliq) and Samarkand.

history.title: Ferghana's wine and the Han envoys
history.text: Chinese envoy Zhang Qian reported that the people of Ferghana made wine from grapes and stored it for years; the Han court brought vines back to China.

history.title: Filatov's Samarkand winery
history.text: A winery was founded in Samarkand, according to its own history, by the merchant D. M. Filatov, shortly after the Russian conquest of the city.

history.title: Khovrenko and Uzbek dessert wines
history.text: Under the oenologist M. A. Khovrenko the Samarkand winery developed sweet and fortified wines that won medals across the USSR; it now bears his name.

country.climate_soils: Hot, dry continental desert-oasis climate with very hot summers, cold winters (vines are often buried) and irrigation from mountain rivers; loess and alluvial soils.

sources.title: OIV, State of the World Wine Sector in 2025

sites.name: Khovrenko winery and museum, Samarkand
sites.text: Samarkand's historic winery at 58 Makhmud Kashgari street, founded in 1868 according to its own history by D. M. Filatov and later named after the Soviet oenologist M. A. Khovrenko. Its museum and tasting room present the sweet and fortified wines and brandies that made Samarkand known in the USSR.

sites.name: Afrasiyab
sites.text: The ancient city mound of Samarkand (Maracanda), capital of Sogdiana, whose merchants traded wine along the Silk Road.
